```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Games live in a local SQLite catalogue. It stores every event of every game,
where each record came from, annotations, and analysis results. Each game is
validated by replaying it through the rules engine before it is stored, and
original files are never modified.

## Open, save, load

```{r}
db_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".sqlite")
db <- gambitR3D::g3_open_game_db(db_path)
db
```

Play two short games and save them. A game that is still running can be
saved again after further moves; the stored record grows in place.

```{r}
play <- function(seed, plies) {
  g <- gambitR3D::g3_new_game(players = list(white = "search", black = "random"))
  g$metadata$agents <- list(white = list(agent = "search"), black = list(agent = "random"))
  for (i in seq_len(plies)) {
    if (gambitR3D::g3_is_terminal(g$state)) break
    agent <- if (g$state$side == "white") "search" else "random"
    d <- gambitR3D::g3_choose_action(g$state, agent, budget = list(nodes = 3000L), seed = seed + i)
    g <- gambitR3D::g3_game_apply(g, d$action_id)
  }
  g
}
g1 <- play(1L, 12L)
g2 <- play(2L, 16L)
s1 <- gambitR3D::g3_save_game(db, g1)
s2 <- gambitR3D::g3_save_game(db, g2)
gambitR3D::g3_query_games(db)[, c("game_id", "status", "white", "black", "plies")]
```

Loading replays the stored events, so the game comes back validated, together
with whether it can be resumed.

```{r}
back <- gambitR3D::g3_load_game(db, s1$game_id)
back$catalogue$status
identical(gambitR3D::g3_game_hash(back), gambitR3D::g3_game_hash(g1))
```

## Query

Filters are data, never code: field names come from a fixed list and values
are bound as parameters.

```{r}
gambitR3D::g3_query_games(db, filters = list(min_plies = 14L, order_by = "plies"))[, c("game_id", "plies")]
gambitR3D::g3_query_games(db, filters = list(player = "Robert'); DROP TABLE games; --"))
```

## Export and import

Export writes the native JSONL format, a manifest with checksums and a
readable move list. PGN and FEN are refused because they would lose the
boards and platforms.

```{r}
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "collection.jsonl")
manifest <- gambitR3D::g3_export_games(db, c(s1$game_id, s2$game_id), out)
manifest$files[, c("file", "role", "records")]
```

Importing a collection gives one report row per record. Importing the same
file twice adds nothing, and a broken record is quarantined with the first
event that fails, while the valid records are still accepted.

```{r}
db2 <- gambitR3D::g3_open_game_db(tempfile(fileext = ".sqlite"))
rep1 <- gambitR3D::g3_import_games(db2, out)
rep1[, c("record", "status")]
rep2 <- gambitR3D::g3_import_games(db2, out)
rep2[, c("record", "status")]

lines <- readLines(out)
broken <- jsonlite::fromJSON(lines[1], simplifyVector = FALSE)
broken$events[[3]]$action_id <- "m:W:0:0-B:3:3"
bad <- file.path(tempdir(), "broken.jsonl")
writeLines(c(as.character(jsonlite::toJSON(broken, auto_unbox = TRUE, null = "null", na = "null", digits = NA)), lines[2]), bad)
rep3 <- gambitR3D::g3_import_games(db2, bad)
rep3[, c("record", "status", "first_invalid_event")]
```

## Backup and integrity

```{r}
bak <- tempfile(fileext = ".sqlite")
b <- gambitR3D::g3_backup_game_db(db, bak)
file.exists(bak)
chk <- gambitR3D::g3_check_game_db(db)
chk$ok
gambitR3D::g3_close_game_db(db)
gambitR3D::g3_close_game_db(db2)
```

A backup uses SQLite's own consistent copy, not a file copy of a live
database. A restore always goes to a new file and is fully replayed before it
is used.

## Read-only use

`g3_open_game_db(path, read_only = TRUE)` never creates, migrates or changes a
file, which makes it the right choice for analysis jobs running beside an app
that is writing.
